title: Ethiopian Chicken Tibs
community: All of Ethiopia — the fast chicken sauté
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Doro Tibs — boneless chicken pieces sautéed fast and hot in kibbeh with onions, jalapeños, tomatoes, rosemary, and berbere. The chicken version of the beloved Ethiopian tibs — faster than Doro Wat, equally satisfying, and irresistibly fragrant.
longDesc: Doro Tibs is the everyday chicken dish for when Doro Wat's 2.5 hours are not available — the same kibbeh, berbere, jalapeño, and rosemary combination that makes beef tibs great, applied to chicken pieces. Done in 20 minutes, it delivers maximum Ethiopian flavour in minimum time.
ingredients: 600g boneless chicken — breast or thigh, cut into pieces
equipment: Cast iron pan or heavy skillet
steps: Heat kibbeh in a heavy pan until smoking hot.
Sear chicken in a single layer — 3 minutes per side.
Add onion. Stir and cook 2 minutes.
Add garlic, jalapeño, and rosemary. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, berbere, black pepper, and salt.
Toss everything together for 2 more minutes.
Chicken should be cooked through — internal temperature 74°C.
chefTips: Chicken thighs are more forgiving than breast — they stay juicier under high heat.
Hot pan is critical — the sear is what develops the flavour.
Check internal temperature — 74°C for food safety.
Serve immediately — Doro Tibs waits for nobody.
commonMistakes: Crowding the pan — chicken steams rather than sears.
cookingScience: Chicken proteins denature at lower temperatures than beef — the myosin in chicken begins denaturing at 50°C, which is why chicken achieves its Maillard crust faster than beef. The rosemary's rosmarinic acid and carnosic acid are antioxidants that protect the chicken's own fats from oxidising during high-heat cooking, maintaining flavour quality.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian free-range chicken — raised on grain and natural forage.
servedWith: As part of a combination platter
culturalNote: Doro Tibs is the everyday miracle of Ethiopian cooking — taking the same ingredients that make the grandest dish (Doro Wat) and applying them in a completely different way to produce something fast, satisfying, and completely its own.
